"""Read models for the Streamlit dashboard (Part 3).

Thin composition over the existing services - no Streamlit import here, so
everything is unit-testable. All statistics are computed from SQLite at call
time via SQLAlchemy (bound parameters); comments are always counted as
COUNT(DISTINCT feedback record) and never as classification rows.

Filter semantics: market / engine type apply to the comment; need category,
VFC category and Feedback Type apply to classification rows, and must all hold
on the same row ("a comment that has at least one classification row with
need X, VFC Y and type Z").
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from core.ai_models import (
    AIFeedbackExtraction,
    CrossSourceEvidenceLink,
    CustomerNeedCategory,
    CustomerNeedCluster,
    VfcNeedMapping,
)
from core.models import CustomerStudy, Feedback, FeedbackClassification, IngestionAudit, SourceDocument
from services.cross_source_mapping import evidence_for_need, vfc_coalesced
from services.customer_insights import StudyValue, sales_context
from services.evidence_retrieval import competitor_evidence, public_owner_feedback
from services.feedback_analysis import (
    CategoryCount,
    DimensionCount,
    FeedbackFilter,
    FeedbackTypeCount,
    SourceReference,
    _joined,
    count_feedback,
    distribution_by,
    feedback_type_distribution,
    filter_conditions,
    vfc_category_counts,
)
from services.need_taxonomy import MISSING_VFC

VEHICLE = "G60"
MISSING_TYPE_LABEL = "(not provided)"


class DashboardFilter(BaseModel):
    countries: list[str] | None = None
    engine_types: list[str] | None = None
    need_codes: list[str] | None = None
    vfc_names: list[str] | None = None  # MISSING_VFC selects empty VFC cells
    feedback_types: list[str | None] | None = None  # None selects missing Feedback Type


def to_feedback_filter(session: Session, f: DashboardFilter) -> FeedbackFilter:
    """Translate need categories into their mapped VFC names and intersect with
    an explicit VFC selection. An empty intersection matches nothing."""
    vfc: set[str] | None = None
    if f.need_codes:
        vfc = set(session.scalars(select(VfcNeedMapping.vfc_level2_name).where(VfcNeedMapping.need_code.in_(f.need_codes))))
    if f.vfc_names:
        vfc = set(f.vfc_names) if vfc is None else vfc & set(f.vfc_names)
    return FeedbackFilter(
        vehicle_code=VEHICLE,
        countries=f.countries or None,
        engine_types=f.engine_types or None,
        feedback_types=f.feedback_types or None,
        vfc_level2=None if vfc is None else sorted((None if v == MISSING_VFC else v) for v in vfc),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Page 1 - Customer Intelligence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class NeedCount(BaseModel):
    need_code: str
    need_name: str
    unique_feedback_count: int
    classification_count: int


class Overview(BaseModel):
    unique_feedback: int
    classification_rows: int
    need_categories_total: int
    need_categories_with_feedback: int
    vfc_clusters_total: int
    vfc_clusters_with_feedback: int
    by_need: list[NeedCount]
    top_vfc: list[CategoryCount]
    by_market: list[DimensionCount]
    by_engine: list[DimensionCount]
    feedback_types: list[FeedbackTypeCount]


def need_category_counts(session: Session, flt: FeedbackFilter) -> list[NeedCount]:
    """Distinct comments per need category (a comment can count in several
    categories when its VFC labels map to different needs)."""
    names = dict(session.execute(select(CustomerNeedCategory.need_code, CustomerNeedCategory.name)).all())
    order = dict(session.execute(select(CustomerNeedCategory.need_code, CustomerNeedCategory.sort_order)).all())
    rows = session.execute(
        _joined(VfcNeedMapping.need_code, func.count(func.distinct(Feedback.record_id)), func.count())
        .join(VfcNeedMapping, VfcNeedMapping.vfc_level2_name == vfc_coalesced())
        .where(*filter_conditions(flt)).group_by(VfcNeedMapping.need_code)
    ).all()
    out = [NeedCount(need_code=c, need_name=names.get(c, c), unique_feedback_count=i, classification_count=r)
           for c, i, r in rows]
    return sorted(out, key=lambda n: (-n.unique_feedback_count, order.get(n.need_code, 99)))


def overview(session: Session, f: DashboardFilter, top_n: int = 15) -> Overview:
    flt = to_feedback_filter(session, f)
    counts = count_feedback(session, flt)
    by_need = need_category_counts(session, flt)
    vfc = vfc_category_counts(session, flt, "level2")
    return Overview(
        unique_feedback=counts.feedback_ids,
        classification_rows=counts.classification_rows,
        need_categories_total=session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(CustomerNeedCategory)) or 0,
        need_categories_with_feedback=sum(1 for n in by_need if n.unique_feedback_count),
        vfc_clusters_total=session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(CustomerNeedCluster).where(
            CustomerNeedCluster.vehicle_code == VEHICLE, CustomerNeedCluster.cluster_level == "vfc_category")) or 0,
        vfc_clusters_with_feedback=sum(1 for c in vfc if c.feedback_ids),
        by_need=by_need,
        # "Topics" exclude rows without a usable class (empty cell / BMW no_class_found).
        top_vfc=[c for c in vfc if c.category not in (None, "no_class_found")][:top_n],
        by_market=distribution_by(session, "country", flt),
        by_engine=distribution_by(session, "engine_type", flt),
        feedback_types=feedback_type_distribution(session, flt),
    )


def filter_options(session: Session) -> dict:
    needs = list(session.execute(select(CustomerNeedCategory.need_code, CustomerNeedCategory.name)
                                 .order_by(CustomerNeedCategory.sort_order)).all())
    vfc = sorted(session.scalars(select(vfc_coalesced()).where(FeedbackClassification.vehicle_code == VEHICLE).distinct()))
    return {
        "countries": sorted(session.scalars(select(Feedback.country).where(Feedback.vehicle_code == VEHICLE).distinct())),
        "engine_types": sorted(session.scalars(select(Feedback.engine_type).where(Feedback.vehicle_code == VEHICLE).distinct())),
        "needs": [{"code": c, "name": n} for c, n in needs],
        "vfc_names": vfc,
        "feedback_types": sorted(
            {t for t in session.scalars(select(FeedbackClassification.feedback_type)
                                        .where(FeedbackClassification.vehicle_code == VEHICLE).distinct())},
            key=lambda t: (t is None, t or "")),
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Page 2 - Evidence Explorer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ClusterOption(BaseModel):
    cluster_id: str
    cluster_level: str
    need_code: str
    label: str
    vfc_level2_name: str | None
    unique_feedback_count: int
    requires_review: bool


def cluster_options(session: Session) -> list[ClusterOption]:
    rows = session.scalars(select(CustomerNeedCluster).where(CustomerNeedCluster.vehicle_code == VEHICLE)
                           .order_by(CustomerNeedCluster.need_code, CustomerNeedCluster.cluster_level,
                                     CustomerNeedCluster.unique_feedback_count.desc())).all()
    return [ClusterOption(cluster_id=c.cluster_id, cluster_level=c.cluster_level, need_code=c.need_code, label=c.label,
                          vfc_level2_name=c.vfc_level2_name, unique_feedback_count=c.unique_feedback_count,
                          requires_review=c.requires_review) for c in rows]


def vfc_mapping_status(session: Session) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str, str | None]]:
    """VFC name -> (need_code, mapping_status, rationale)."""
    return {m.vfc_level2_name: (m.need_code, m.mapping_status, m.rationale) for m in session.scalars(select(VfcNeedMapping))}


class EvidenceItem(BaseModel):
    tier: str  # SUPPORTING | CONTEXTUAL
    kind: str  # public_owner_feedback | public_bmw_observation | customer_study | competitor_observation
    key: str
    title: str
    detail: str | None
    source_url: str | None
    requires_review: bool
    mapping_note: str | None
    source: SourceReference
    study_values: list[StudyValue] = []


def related_evidence(session: Session, need_code: str) -> list[EvidenceItem]:
    """Supporting and contextual evidence for a need, resolved to source records.
    Direct evidence (internal feedback) is listed separately by the caller."""
    ev = evidence_for_need(session, need_code, VEHICLE)
    competitor = {c.source.source_row: c for c in competitor_evidence(session)}
    items: list[EvidenceItem] = []
    for link in ev.supporting + ev.contextual:
        tier = link.evidence_tier.upper()
        if link.source_table == "public_feedback":
            p = public_owner_feedback(session, public_id=link.source_key)[0]
            items.append(EvidenceItem(
                tier=tier, kind="public_owner_feedback", key=p.original_public_id,
                title=f"{p.original_public_id} · {p.model} · {p.market} · {p.theme}",
                detail=f"{p.paraphrased_feedback} (sentiment as labelled in source: {p.sentiment_as_labelled_in_source}; "
                       f"note: {p.evidence_note})",
                source_url=p.source_url, requires_review=link.requires_review, mapping_note=link.note, source=p.source))
        elif link.source_table == "competitor_evidence":
            c = competitor[int(link.source_key.removeprefix("COMP-R"))]
            items.append(EvidenceItem(
                tier=tier, kind="public_bmw_observation" if c.is_bmw else "competitor_observation", key=link.source_key,
                title=f"{c.brand} {c.model} · {c.market} · {c.theme}",
                detail=f"{c.extracted_insight} (limitation: {c.evidence_limitation}; sentiment as labelled: "
                       f"{c.sentiment_as_labelled_in_source})",
                source_url=c.source_url, requires_review=link.requires_review, mapping_note=link.note, source=c.source))
        elif link.source_table == "customer_studies":
            cells = study_cells(session, link.record_ids)
            first = cells[0].source if cells else None
            items.append(EvidenceItem(
                tier=tier, kind="customer_study", key=link.source_key, title=link.source_label, detail=None,
                source_url=None, requires_review=link.requires_review, mapping_note=link.note,
                source=first or SourceReference(record_id="", source_file="", source_sheet=None, source_row=None,
                                                data_origin="internal_bmw"),
                study_values=cells))
    return items


def study_cells(session: Session, record_ids: list[str]) -> list[StudyValue]:
    rows = session.scalars(select(CustomerStudy).where(CustomerStudy.record_id.in_(record_ids))
                           .order_by(CustomerStudy.source_row, CustomerStudy.source_column)).all()
    return [StudyValue(study_name=r.study_name, survey_market=r.survey_market, vehicle_label=r.vehicle_label,
                       vehicle_code=r.vehicle_code, attribute=r.attribute, measure=r.measure, value_type=r.value_type,
                       value=r.value, source=SourceReference(record_id=r.record_id, source_file=r.source_file,
                                                             source_sheet=r.source_sheet, source_row=r.source_row,
                                                             data_origin="internal_bmw"))
            for r in rows]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Page 4 - Data Quality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def source_documents(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    return [{"file": d.file_name, "dataset_type": d.dataset_type, "origin": d.data_origin, "type": d.file_type,
             "source_of_truth": d.is_source_of_truth, "status": d.ingestion_status,
             "original_names": ", ".join(json.loads(d.original_file_names or "[]")), "notes": d.ingestion_notes or ""}
            for d in session.scalars(select(SourceDocument).order_by(SourceDocument.data_origin, SourceDocument.file_name))]


def audit_rows(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    """Count checks recorded at the last ingestion (raw-file recount vs database)."""
    return [{"file": a.source_file, "sheet": a.source_sheet, "table": a.target_table, "expected": a.expected_count,
             "imported": a.imported_count, "basis": a.count_basis, "status": a.status, "checked_at": a.checked_at}
            for a in session.scalars(select(IngestionAudit).order_by(IngestionAudit.audit_id))]


def review_mappings(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    """VFC -> need mappings still marked review_required, with G60 comment counts."""
    counts = dict(session.execute(
        select(vfc_coalesced(), func.count(func.distinct(FeedbackClassification.feedback_record_id)))
        .where(FeedbackClassification.vehicle_code == VEHICLE).group_by(vfc_coalesced())).all())
    return sorted(({"vfc_level2_name": m.vfc_level2_name, "need_code": m.need_code, "reason": m.rationale,
                    "g60_comments": counts.get(m.vfc_level2_name, 0)}
                   for m in session.scalars(select(VfcNeedMapping).where(VfcNeedMapping.mapping_status == "review_required"))),
                  key=lambda r: -r["g60_comments"])


def review_links(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    return [{"need_code": l.need_code, "tier": l.evidence_tier, "source_table": l.source_table, "source_key": l.source_key,
             "label": l.source_label, "note": l.note}
            for l in session.scalars(select(CrossSourceEvidenceLink).where(
                CrossSourceEvidenceLink.requires_review.is_(True), CrossSourceEvidenceLink.evidence_tier != "direct")
                .order_by(CrossSourceEvidenceLink.need_code, CrossSourceEvidenceLink.link_id))]


class Limitation(BaseModel):
    title: str
    evidence: str  # computed from the database


def known_limitations(session: Session) -> list[Limitation]:
    """The eight known limitations, each with a figure computed live."""
    fc = FeedbackClassification
    likes = select(fc.feedback_record_id).where(fc.vehicle_code == VEHICLE, fc.feedback_type == "Likes")
    both = session.scalar(select(func.count(func.distinct(fc.feedback_record_id))).where(
        fc.vehicle_code == VEHICLE, fc.feedback_type.in_(["Defect", "Difficult to Use"]), fc.feedback_record_id.in_(likes))) or 0
    missing_type = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(fc).where(fc.vehicle_code == VEHICLE, fc.feedback_type.is_(None))) or 0
    multi = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Feedback).where(
        Feedback.vehicle_code == VEHICLE, Feedback.classification_row_count > 1)) or 0
    total = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Feedback).where(Feedback.vehicle_code == VEHICLE)) or 0
    markets = distribution_by(session, "country", FeedbackFilter(vehicle_code=VEHICLE))
    top = markets[0] if markets else None
    public_n = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(CrossSourceEvidenceLink.__table__.metadata.tables["public_feedback"]
                                                                 if False else Feedback).where(False)) if False else None
    from core.models import PublicFeedback  # local: only used here

    public_n = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(PublicFeedback)) or 0
    sales = sales_context(session, VEHICLE)
    review_n = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(CrossSourceEvidenceLink).where(
        CrossSourceEvidenceLink.requires_review.is_(True))) or 0
    links_n = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(CrossSourceEvidenceLink)) or 0
    extractions = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(AIFeedbackExtraction).where(
        AIFeedbackExtraction.status == "succeeded", AIFeedbackExtraction.vehicle_code == VEHICLE)) or 0
    return [
        Limitation(title="Feedback Type is not reliable sentiment",
                   evidence=f"{both} G60 comments carry both a 'Likes' row and a 'Defect'/'Difficult to Use' row; "
                            f"{missing_type} classification rows have no Feedback Type. No sentiment shares are shown."),
        Limitation(title="Some comments have multiple VFC classifications",
                   evidence=f"{multi} of {total} G60 comments have more than one classification row; "
                            "comment counts use COUNT(DISTINCT feedback)."),
        Limitation(title="Most feedback originates from the US",
                   evidence=(f"{top.value}: {top.feedback_ids} of {total} comments ({top.share_of_feedback_ids:.0%})."
                             if top else "No market data.")),
        Limitation(title="Public feedback is small and curated",
                   evidence=f"{public_n} paraphrased public observations; several rows can come from one review; "
                            "not a representative sample."),
        Limitation(title="Survey sample sizes are unavailable",
                   evidence="The customer-study workbook provides means (CN/EU) and answer proportions (US) only; "
                            "no respondent counts are stored or inferred."),
        Limitation(title="G60/G68 sales are combined",
                   evidence=" ".join(sales.warnings[:1]) or "No combined sales rows found."),
        Limitation(title="Some cross-source mappings require review",
                   evidence=f"{review_n} of {links_n} cross-source evidence links are marked requires_review."),
        Limitation(title="No real LLM extraction has run yet" if extractions == 0 else "LLM extraction coverage is partial",
                   evidence=(f"{extractions} AI extractions stored. All insights are deterministic templates built from "
                             "original VFC classifications." if extractions == 0 else
                             f"{extractions} of {total} G60 comments have stored AI extractions.")),
    ]

"""Part 3 dashboard tests: data layer against raw files, stable IDs, and each
Streamlit page loading on a real-data database copy. No LLM calls."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select

from core import config
from core.ai_models import CustomerNeedCluster, GeneratedCustomerInsight
from core.database import ensure_ai_schema, get_engine, session_scope
from services import dashboard_queries as dq
from services.cross_source_mapping import build_cross_source_links
from services.insight_generator import STATUS_TEMPLATE, all_insight_cards, generate_insights
from services.need_clustering import build_clusters, vfc_cluster_id
from services.need_taxonomy import MISSING_VFC, sync_taxonomy, vfc_mapping

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def dash_db(built, tmp_path_factory):
    """Real-data DB with the Part 2 deterministic layer built (no LLM)."""
    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("dash") / "dash.db"
    shutil.copy2(built["db_path"], path)
    engine = get_engine(path)
    ensure_ai_schema(engine)
    with session_scope(engine) as s:
        sync_taxonomy(s)
        build_cross_source_links(s)
        build_clusters(s)
        generate_insights(s, min_unique_feedback=10)
    engine.dispose()
    return path


@pytest.fixture()
def s(dash_db):
    engine = get_engine(dash_db)
    with session_scope(engine) as session:
        yield session
    engine.dispose()


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def raw(data_dir):
    df = pd.read_excel(next(data_dir.rglob(config.FEEDBACK_FILES["G60"])), sheet_name=config.FEEDBACK_SHEET, dtype=object)
    mapping = {n: code for n, (code, _, _) in vfc_mapping().items()}
    df["vfc_key"] = df["Vfc level2 Name"].map(lambda v: MISSING_VFC if pd.isna(v) else v)
    df["need"] = df["vfc_key"].map(mapping)
    return df


# --- counts -----------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_overview_counts_match_source(s, raw):
    o = dq.overview(s, dq.DashboardFilter())
    assert o.unique_feedback == raw["ID"].nunique() == 4000
    assert o.classification_rows == len(raw) == 5005
    assert o.need_categories_total == 18 and o.vfc_clusters_total == 222
    assert {n.need_code: n.unique_feedback_count for n in o.by_need} == raw.groupby("need")["ID"].nunique().to_dict()
    assert {d.value: d.feedback_ids for d in o.by_market} == raw.drop_duplicates("ID")["Country"].value_counts().to_dict()
    assert {d.value: d.feedback_ids for d in o.by_engine} == raw.drop_duplicates("ID")["Engine Type"].value_counts().to_dict()
    top = raw[~raw["vfc_key"].isin([MISSING_VFC, "no_class_found"])].groupby("vfc_key")["ID"].nunique()
    assert [c.feedback_ids for c in o.top_vfc] == sorted(top.to_list(), reverse=True)[:15]


def test_comments_are_never_counted_as_classifications(s, raw):
    o = dq.overview(s, dq.DashboardFilter(vfc_names=["Touch screen, operation"]))
    rows = raw[raw["vfc_key"] == "Touch screen, operation"]
    assert o.unique_feedback == rows["ID"].nunique() and o.classification_rows == len(rows)
    assert o.unique_feedback < o.classification_rows  # a comment with 2 such rows counts once
    total = dq.overview(s, dq.DashboardFilter())
    assert sum(d.feedback_ids for d in total.by_market) == total.unique_feedback  # markets partition comments


@pytest.mark.parametrize("f, mask", [
    (dq.DashboardFilter(countries=["US"], engine_types=["BEVE"]),
     lambda d: (d["Country"] == "US") & (d["Engine Type"] == "BEVE")),
    (dq.DashboardFilter(need_codes=["CONTROLS"], feedback_types=["Difficult to Use"]),
     lambda d: (d["need"] == "CONTROLS") & (d["Feedback Type"] == "Difficult to Use")),
    (dq.DashboardFilter(countries=["US"], engine_types=["BEVE"], need_codes=["CONTROLS"], feedback_types=["Difficult to Use"]),
     lambda d: (d["Country"] == "US") & (d["Engine Type"] == "BEVE") & (d["need"] == "CONTROLS")
     & (d["Feedback Type"] == "Difficult to Use")),
    (dq.DashboardFilter(need_codes=["CONTROLS"], vfc_names=["Touch screen, operation"]),
     lambda d: d["vfc_key"] == "Touch screen, operation"),
    (dq.DashboardFilter(feedback_types=[None]), lambda d: d["Feedback Type"].isna()),
    (dq.DashboardFilter(vfc_names=[MISSING_VFC]), lambda d: d["vfc_key"] == MISSING_VFC),
])
def test_filters_combine_correctly(s, raw, f, mask):
    subset = raw[mask(raw)]
    o = dq.overview(s, f)
    assert o.unique_feedback == subset["ID"].nunique()
    assert o.classification_rows == len(subset)


def test_contradictory_filters_return_empty_gracefully(s):
    o = dq.overview(s, dq.DashboardFilter(need_codes=["CHARGING"], vfc_names=["Touch screen, operation"]))
    assert o.unique_feedback == 0 and o.by_need == [] and o.top_vfc == []


# --- evidence ---------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_insight_evidence_ids_resolve_to_original_comments(s, raw):
    texts = raw.drop_duplicates("ID").set_index("ID")["Customer Feedback"].to_dict()
    from services.evidence_retrieval import get_feedback_by_ids

    for card in all_insight_cards(s)[:10]:
        records = get_feedback_by_ids(s, card.internal_evidence_ids)
        assert [r.original_feedback_id for r in records] == card.internal_evidence_ids
        assert all(r.customer_feedback == texts[r.original_feedback_id] for r in records)
        assert all(r.source.source_file == config.FEEDBACK_FILES["G60"] and r.source.source_row for r in records)


def test_public_and_internal_evidence_stay_separate(s):
    for need in ("CONTROLS", "INFOTAINMENT", "CHARGING"):
        for item in dq.related_evidence(s, need):
            assert item.tier in ("SUPPORTING", "CONTEXTUAL")
            if item.kind == "public_owner_feedback":
                assert item.source.data_origin == "public_external" and item.source_url and item.tier == "SUPPORTING"
            if item.kind == "competitor_observation":
                assert item.tier == "CONTEXTUAL" and item.source.data_origin == "public_external"
            if item.kind == "customer_study":
                assert item.study_values and all(v.vehicle_code == "G60" for v in item.study_values)
            assert item.source.source_file and item.source.source_row


# --- insights ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_template_insights_are_labelled_template(s):
    cards = all_insight_cards(s)
    assert len(cards) == s.query(GeneratedCustomerInsight).count() > 0
    assert {c.status for c in cards} == {STATUS_TEMPLATE}  # no extraction has run in this DB
    assert all(c.text_source == "deterministic_template" for c in cards)


# --- stable identifiers ---------------------------------------------------------------


def test_cluster_and_insight_ids_are_stable_across_rebuilds(s):
    def snapshot():
        clusters = {c.cluster_id: (c.cluster_level, c.need_code, c.vfc_level2_name, c.unique_feedback_count)
                    for c in s.scalars(select(CustomerNeedCluster))}
        insights = {i.insight_id: (i.cluster_id, i.internal_evidence_ids_json)
                    for i in s.scalars(select(GeneratedCustomerInsight))}
        return clusters, insights

    before = snapshot()
    build_clusters(s)
    generate_insights(s, min_unique_feedback=10)
    s.flush()
    assert snapshot() == before
    c = s.scalar(select(CustomerNeedCluster).where(CustomerNeedCluster.vfc_level2_name == "Touch screen, operation"))
    assert c.cluster_id == vfc_cluster_id("Touch screen, operation")
    assert s.get(GeneratedCustomerInsight, f"INS-{c.cluster_id}") is not None
    s.rollback()


def test_known_limitations_are_computed(s):
    lims = dq.known_limitations(s)
    assert len(lims) == 8
    assert lims[-1].title == "No real LLM extraction has run yet"
    assert "US: 3610 of 4000" in lims[2].evidence


# --- Streamlit pages --------------------------------------------------------------------


PAGES = ["ui/pages/customer_intelligence.py", "ui/pages/evidence_explorer.py",
         "ui/pages/customer_insights.py", "ui/pages/data_quality.py"]


@pytest.fixture()
def app(dash_db, monkeypatch):
    from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

    monkeypatch.setenv("PRODUCTMIND_DB_PATH", str(dash_db))

    def forbid(*a, **k):
        raise AssertionError("The dashboard must not construct an LLM client")

    monkeypatch.setattr("services.llm_client.AnthropicLLMClient.__init__", forbid)
    monkeypatch.setattr("anthropic.Anthropic.__init__", forbid, raising=False)
    import streamlit as st

    st.cache_data.clear()
    st.cache_resource.clear()
    at = AppTest.from_file(str(ROOT / "app.py"), default_timeout=180)
    return at


def test_every_page_loads_without_errors(app):
    app.run()
    assert not app.exception
    for page in PAGES[1:]:
        app.switch_page(page).run()
        assert not app.exception, (page, [e.value for e in app.exception])


def test_overview_page_shows_database_counts(app):
    app.run()
    html = " ".join(m.value for m in app.markdown)
    assert "4,000" in html and "5,005" in html and "18 / 18" in html and "222 / 222" in html
    assert "sentiment" not in " ".join(m.value for m in app.markdown if "pm-kpi" in m.value).lower()


def test_overview_filters_update_counts(app, raw):
    app.run()
    app.multiselect(key="ci_market").set_value(["KR"]).run()
    expected = raw[raw["Country"] == "KR"]["ID"].nunique()
    assert f'class="v">{expected:,}<' in " ".join(m.value for m in app.markdown)


def test_insights_page_labels_templates_and_links_to_explorer(app):
    app.switch_page("ui/pages/customer_insights.py").run()
    text = " ".join(m.value for m in app.markdown) + " ".join(i.value for i in app.info)
    assert "TEMPLATE" in text and "Nothing here is an AI-generated finding" in text
    assert "AI_ENRICHED · uses LLM extraction" not in text  # no card carries the AI badge
    buttons = [b for b in app.button if b.label == "View Supporting Evidence"]
    assert buttons
    target = buttons[0].key.removeprefix("view_INS-")
    buttons[0].click().run()
    assert not app.exception
    assert app.session_state["ex_cluster"] == target


def test_explorer_marks_review_items_and_tiers(app):
    app.switch_page("ui/pages/evidence_explorer.py").run()
    app.selectbox(key="ex_need").set_value("CONTROLS").run()
    html = " ".join(m.value for m in app.markdown)
    assert "Direct · internal BMW feedback" in html
    assert "Supporting · public BMW feedback / BMW study" in html
    assert any("requires review" in w.value for w in app.warning)
    assert "pm-src" in html  # source references rendered


def test_dashboard_code_never_references_llm_pipeline():
    sources = [p.read_text() for p in (ROOT / "ui").rglob("*.py")] + [(ROOT / "app.py").read_text(),
                                                                       (ROOT / "services/dashboard_queries.py").read_text()]
    for src in sources:
        for forbidden in ("AnthropicLLMClient", "run_extraction", "import anthropic", "llm_client"):
            assert forbidden not in src

content.text:
Part 3 is finished: run `streamlit run app.py` to open the dashboard. All 95 tests pass (75 existing plus 20 new). I also checked every page in a real browser, and no LLM calls were made (the database still has 0 API calls logged).

**Pages implemented**
- **Customer Intelligence:**
  - Four headline numbers: 4,000 unique comments, 5,005 classification records, and 18/18 categories and 222/222 VFC clusters with matching feedback.
  - Charts of comments by need category, top VFC topics, market and engine type, each with a table view.
  - All five filters combine. Need category, VFC category and Feedback Type must match on the same classification row.
  - Feedback Type appears only as raw counts labelled "not sentiment"; no positive/negative shares anywhere.
- **Evidence Explorer:**
  - Pick a need category or VFC cluster, then browse expandable comment cards. Each card shows the full text, ID, VFC labels, market, engine type and the source file/sheet/row.
  - Literal text search, sidebar filters and pagination.
  - Separate Direct, Supporting and Contextual tabs, with source URLs and a visible warning on any mapping that needs review.
- **Customer Insights:**
  - All 101 insights carry the status TEMPLATE, with a banner saying nothing on the page is an AI-generated finding. The status is worked out from the database, so AI_ENRICHED only appears once real LLM extraction exists.
  - On template cards I renamed the "Customer problem" field to "Original VFC level-3 labels". Those labels are often praise (e.g. "Like: performance"), so calling them a problem was misleading.
  - "View Supporting Evidence" opens the Explorer on that cluster. I clicked it in the browser: "Handling / Riding" opened with its 226 comments.
- **Data Quality:**
  - Imported datasets, live record counts, 7/7 integrity checks and 22/22 raw-file count checks.
  - Missing data, the 62 VFC mappings and 44 evidence links still awaiting review, and your 8 limitations, each with a live figure (e.g. "US: 3,610 of 4,000 comments (90%)").

**Stable cluster IDs.** The old `CLUSTER-001`-style IDs changed whenever clusters were rebuilt. IDs now come from fixed keys:
- `NEED-CONTROLS` for need categories;
- `VFC-` plus a hash of the original VFC name;
- `INS-` plus the cluster ID for insights.

A test rebuilds everything and confirms that every cluster and insight ID, and its links, stays the same. The real database now uses only the new IDs.

**Tests.** The 20 new dashboard tests run on a copy of the real database and check:
- **Counts and filters:** counts and six filter combinations against pandas on the raw file; comments never counted as classification rows; impossible filter combinations shown as empty.
- **Evidence:** evidence IDs resolve to the original comment text; public and internal evidence stay separate; templates are labelled correctly.
- **Pages:** each page loads; filter changes update the numbers; the insight button navigates to the right cluster.
- **No LLM use:** the dashboard is blocked from creating an LLM client, and its code is checked for any reference to the extraction pipeline.

**Other changes**
- `app.py` is now the Streamlit entry point. The old command-line status view moved to `python -m scripts.status`.
- `streamlit` and `plotly` are added to `requirements.txt`, and the README has a dashboard section.

**Remaining issues**
- The insights are only as informative as the VFC labels until a real extraction runs. That still needs an API key and your OK to send the feedback to an external API.
- Supporting and contextual evidence is linked per need category, not per comment or VFC cluster. The Explorer says so on screen.
- 62 VFC mappings and 44 evidence links still need a human review.
- Most feedback is from the US, so the other markets have very few comments.

"""Vehicle-requirement tables (Part 4).

Registered on ``AIBase``: created/migrated additively by
``core.database.ensure_ai_schema`` and never dropped by ingestion rebuilds.
Requirement IDs are generated once (UUID-based) and stored, so they survive
application restarts, cluster rebuilds and ingestion rebuilds.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, DateTime, ForeignKey, Integer, String, Text, UniqueConstraint
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from core.ai_models import AIBase

GENERATION_METHODS = ("RULE_BASED", "LLM_ASSISTED", "HUMAN_AUTHORED")
REVIEW_STATUSES = ("DRAFT", "PENDING_REVIEW", "APPROVED", "REJECTED")


class VehicleRequirement(AIBase):
    __tablename__ = "vehicle_requirements"

input.content:
"""Evidence package for requirement generation (Part 4).

Given a cluster (need category ``NEED-*``, VFC category ``VFC-*`` or AI need
``XN-*``) or an insight, assemble everything a requirement may cite, using
actual database IDs only:

* DIRECT      the cluster's original G60 comments (cluster members)
* SUPPORTING  public BMW owner observations and BMW customer-study items,
              linked at NEED-CATEGORY level (never proof of a specific complaint)
* CONTEXTUAL  competitor observations and G60 option-list equipment

Reuses Part 2/3 services (insight facts, cross-source evidence, retrieval).
New queries here: equipment context, and distinct comments per VFC level-3
label group.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from core.ai_models import CustomerNeedCluster, GeneratedCustomerInsight, VfcNeedMapping
from core.models import Equipment, FeedbackClassification
from services.cross_source_mapping import vfc_coalesced
from services.dashboard_queries import EvidenceItem, related_evidence
from services.evidence_retrieval import get_feedback_by_ids
from services.insight_generator import build_facts, insight_id_for
from services.need_taxonomy import MISSING_VFC, NEED_NAMES

VEHICLE = "G60"
DIRECT_PREVIEW = 25
OPTION_LIST_NOTE = ("G60 option list (German market, July 2026 edition): shows what is currently offered and at "
                    "which price, not customer evidence.")

# Curated: which option-list sections / SA codes give equipment context for a need.
EQUIPMENT_CONTEXT: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {
    "DRIVER_ASSISTANCE": {"sections": ["FAHRASSISTENZ UND SICHERHEIT"], "codes": []},
    "CLIMATE": {"sections": ["KLIMAKOMFORT"], "codes": ["248"]},
    "INFOTAINMENT": {"sections": ["KONNEKTIVITÄT UND INFOTAINMENT"], "codes": []},
    "DRIVING_DYNAMICS": {"sections": ["ANTRIEB / FAHRDYNAMIK / FAHRWERK"], "codes": ["704"]},
    "INTERIOR_COMFORT": {"sections": ["SITZKOMFORT"], "codes": ["4MA"]},
    "INTERIOR_QUALITY": {"sections": ["INTERIEUR", "INTERIEURLEISTEN"], "codes": []},
    "PRACTICALITY": {"sections": ["TRANSPORT UND STAURAUM"], "codes": []},
    "EXTERIOR": {"sections": ["EXTERIEUR"], "codes": []},
    "CHARGING": {"sections": [], "codes": ["4U6"]},
}

# Original BMW VFC level-3 labels grouped by what they describe (not sentiment).
POSITIVE_LABELS = {"Look / design appeals", "Likes comfort", "Likes size", "Workmanship appeals"}
CATCH_ALL_VFC = {"Exterior", "Interior", "Accessories / Parts", "General enquiry: customer feedback", "no_class_found",
                 MISSING_VFC}


def label_group(label: str | None) -> str:
    if not label:
        return "unlabelled"
    if label.startswith("Like") or label in POSITIVE_LABELS:
        return "positive"
    if label.startswith("Customer request"):
        return "request"
    return "issue"


class DirectItem(BaseModel):
    feedback_id: str
    record_id: str
    source_file: str
    source_sheet: str | None
    source_row: int | None
    country: str | None
    engine_type: str | None
    text: str
    vfc_labels: list[str]


class EquipmentItem(BaseModel):
    option_code: str
    name: str | None
    section: str | None
    price_gross_eur_text: str | None
    source_file: str
    source_page: int | None
    record_id: str


class EvidencePackage(BaseModel):
    cluster_id: str
    cluster_level: str
    cluster_label: str
    vfc_level2_name: str | None
    need_code: str
    need_name: str
    vehicle_code: str
    insight_id: str | None
    unique_feedback_count: int
    classification_count: int
    markets: list[dict]
    vfc_level3_labels: list[dict]
    label_groups: dict[str, int]  # distinct comments per label group (a comment can be in several)
    direct_feedback_ids: list[str]
    direct_evidence: list[DirectItem]  # preview with full text and source refs
    supporting_evidence: list[EvidenceItem]
    contextual_evidence: list[EvidenceItem]
    equipment_context: list[EquipmentItem]
    mapping_requires_review: bool
    mapping_note: str | None
    extracted_need_count: int
    limitations: list[str]
    missing_evidence: list[str]


def _cluster(session: Session, cluster_id: str) -> CustomerNeedCluster:
    cluster = session.get(CustomerNeedCluster, cluster_id)
    if cluster is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown cluster {cluster_id!r}")
    if cluster.vehicle_code != VEHICLE:
        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_id} is not a {VEHICLE} cluster")
    return cluster


def cluster_for_insight(session: Session, insight_id: str) -> str:
    insight = session.get(GeneratedCustomerInsight, insight_id)
    if insight is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown insight {insight_id!r}")
    return insight.cluster_id


def equipment_context(session: Session, need_code: str) -> list[EquipmentItem]:
    spec = EQUIPMENT_CONTEXT.get(need_code)
    if not spec:
        return []
    cond = Equipment.section.in_(spec["sections"])
    if spec["codes"]:
        cond = cond | Equipment.option_code.in_(spec["codes"])
    rows = session.scalars(select(Equipment).where(Equipment.vehicle_code == VEHICLE, cond)
                           .order_by(Equipment.source_page, Equipment.option_code)).all()
    seen, out = set(), []
    for e in rows:
        if e.option_code in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(e.option_code)
        out.append(EquipmentItem(option_code=e.option_code, name=e.name, section=e.section,
                                 price_gross_eur_text=e.price_gross_eur_text, source_file=e.source_file,
                                 source_page=e.source_page, record_id=e.record_id))
    return out


def _label_groups(session: Session, member_ids: list[str], scope: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
    from core.models import Feedback

    rows = session.execute(
        select(FeedbackClassification.feedback_record_id, FeedbackClassification.vfc_level3_name)
        .join(Feedback, Feedback.record_id == FeedbackClassification.feedback_record_id)
        .where(Feedback.original_feedback_id.in_(member_ids), Feedback.vehicle_code == VEHICLE,
               vfc_coalesced().in_(scope))).all()
    groups: dict[str, set[str]] = {"issue": set(), "request": set(), "positive": set(), "unlabelled": set()}
    for rid, label in rows:
        groups[label_group(label)].add(rid)
    return {k: len(v) for k, v in groups.items()}


def build_evidence_package(session: Session, *, cluster_id: str | None = None, insight_id: str | None = None,
                           need_code: str | None = None) -> EvidencePackage:
    """Exactly one selector: a cluster, an insight, or a whole need category."""
    if sum(x is not None for x in (cluster_id, insight_id, need_code)) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Pass exactly one of cluster_id, insight_id, need_code")
    if insight_id:
        cluster_id = cluster_for_insight(session, insight_id)
    if need_code:
        cluster_id = f"NEED-{need_code}"
    cluster = _cluster(session, cluster_id)
    facts = build_facts(session, cluster)  # SQL-computed counts, members, markets, links, limitations

    if cluster.vfc_level2_name is not None:
        scope = [cluster.vfc_level2_name]
    else:
        scope = list(session.scalars(select(VfcNeedMapping.vfc_level2_name)
                                     .where(VfcNeedMapping.need_code == cluster.need_code)))
    mapping = session.get(VfcNeedMapping, cluster.vfc_level2_name) if cluster.vfc_level2_name else None

    records = get_feedback_by_ids(session, facts.internal_evidence_ids[:DIRECT_PREVIEW], VEHICLE)
    direct = [DirectItem(feedback_id=r.original_feedback_id, record_id=r.source.record_id, source_file=r.source.source_file,
                         source_sheet=r.source.source_sheet, source_row=r.source.source_row, country=r.country,
                         engine_type=r.engine_type, text=r.customer_feedback,
                         vfc_labels=[c.vfc_level2_3_name or "(empty VFC cell)" for c in r.classifications])
              for r in records]

    linked = related_evidence(session, cluster.need_code)
    supporting = [i for i in linked if i.tier == "SUPPORTING"]
    contextual = [i for i in linked if i.tier == "CONTEXTUAL"]
    equipment = equipment_context(session, cluster.need_code)
    insight = session.get(GeneratedCustomerInsight, insight_id_for(cluster.cluster_id))

    missing: list[str] = []
    if facts.unique_feedback_count < 5:
        missing.append(f"Only {facts.unique_feedback_count} direct comments - too few to define a specific requirement.")
    if not facts.extracted_needs:
        missing.append("No AI extraction of customer wording: the customer need is derived from VFC labels only.")
    if not any(i.kind in ("public_owner_feedback", "public_bmw_observation") for i in supporting):
        missing.append("No public BMW owner observation is mapped to this need.")
    if not any(i.kind == "customer_study" for i in supporting):
        missing.append("No customer-study attribute is mapped to this need.")
    if not equipment:
        missing.append("No G60 option-list equipment context is mapped to this need.")
    if cluster.cluster_level == "need_category":
        missing.append("Need-category selection spans several VFC classes; the affected function is not specific.")
    if (cluster.vfc_level2_name or "") in CATCH_ALL_VFC or "overall technology" in (cluster.vfc_level2_name or ""):
        missing.append("VFC class is a broad catch-all; the affected function is not specific.")
    review_items = [i.key for i in supporting + contextual if i.requires_review]
    if review_items:
        missing.append(f"{len(review_items)} linked supporting/contextual items have uncertain mappings (requires review).")

    return EvidencePackage(
        cluster_id=cluster.cluster_id, cluster_level=cluster.cluster_level, cluster_label=cluster.label,
        vfc_level2_name=cluster.vfc_level2_name, need_code=cluster.need_code, need_name=NEED_NAMES[cluster.need_code],
        vehicle_code=VEHICLE, insight_id=insight.insight_id if insight else None,
        unique_feedback_count=facts.unique_feedback_count, classification_count=facts.classification_count,
        markets=facts.markets, vfc_level3_labels=facts.vfc_level3_labels,
        label_groups=_label_groups(session, facts.internal_evidence_ids, scope),
        direct_feedback_ids=facts.internal_evidence_ids, direct_evidence=direct, supporting_evidence=supporting,
        contextual_evidence=contextual, equipment_context=equipment,
        mapping_requires_review=bool(cluster.requires_review), mapping_note=(mapping.rationale if mapping else cluster.review_note),
        extracted_need_count=len(facts.extracted_needs),
        limitations=facts.limitations + [OPTION_LIST_NOTE] * bool(equipment),
        missing_evidence=missing,
    )

"""Requirement draft generation (Part 4).

MODE A - RULE_BASED (default, offline, no API key)
    Category-specific, solution-neutral templates filled ONLY with values from
    the evidence package. Framing is decided from the distinct-comment counts
    of the original VFC level-3 label groups:
      * improve  - issue/request labels are a substantial share
      * retain   - comments are predominantly positive labels
      * refine   - selection is broad/ambiguous or evidence is thin: a
                   problem-oriented draft is produced, marked as requiring
                   refinement, with the missing information listed. No
                   technical solution is proposed.
    Acceptance criteria name a measurement method; targets are always
    "proposed - requires validation". No BMW specifications are invented.

MODE B - LLM_ASSISTED (optional, disabled by default)
    Only runs when ALL hold: PRODUCTMIND_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_LLM is set, an API key
    is present, the caller passes ``confirmed=True`` and acknowledges the
    displayed cost estimate. Server-side model fallback is forced off.
    The model writes text fields only; evidence IDs and counts are attached by
    code and the result goes through the same validator.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from core.config import LLMSettings, get_llm_settings
from services.need_taxonomy import NEED_NAMES
from services.requirement_evidence import CATCH_ALL_VFC, EvidencePackage

VEHICLE_MODEL = "BMW 5 Series (G60)"
TARGET_GENERATION = "Next-generation BMW 5 Series (successor to G60; launch timing not assumed)"
PROPOSED_TARGET = "Proposed target - requires validation (no target derivable from the available evidence)"
MIN_COMMENTS_FOR_SPECIFIC = 5


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Draft model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AcceptanceCriterion(BaseModel):
    criterion: str
    measurement: str
    target: str = PROPOSED_TARGET
    target_status: str = "proposed_requires_validation"  # | evidence_baseline


class EvidenceRef(BaseModel):
    tier: str  # DIRECT | SUPPORTING | CONTEXTUAL
    source_table: str
    source_key: str
    source_record_id: str | None
    evidence_scope: str  # cluster_member | need_category | vehicle_catalogue
    requires_review: bool = False
    note: str | None = None


class RequirementDraft(BaseModel):
    title: str
    source_cluster_id: str
    source_insight_id: str | None
    need_code: str
    customer_need: str
    customer_problem: str
    proposed_requirement: str
    requirement_type: str
    vehicle_model: str = VEHICLE_MODEL
    source_vehicle_code: str = "G60"
    target_generation: str = TARGET_GENERATION
    evidence_summary: str
    assumptions: list[str]
    acceptance_criteria: list[AcceptanceCriterion]
    generation_method: str = "RULE_BASED"
    template_id: str | None = None
    framing: str  # improve | retain | refine
    requires_refinement: bool = False
    refinement_notes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    evidence: list[EvidenceRef]
    allowed_numbers: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # numbers that come from the evidence package

    def supporting_evidence_ids(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        out: dict[str, list[str]] = {"direct": [], "supporting": [], "contextual": []}
        for e in self.evidence:
            out[e.tier.lower()].append(e.source_key)
        return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Category templates (solution-neutral)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Template:
    requirement_type: str
    value: str        # what customers value, as a need phrase
    issue_kind: str   # how issues in this category are described
    measurement: str  # how fulfilment would be measured (method, not target)


TEMPLATES: dict[str, Template] = {
    "INFOTAINMENT": Template("functional_usability", "dependable, easy-to-use infotainment and digital functions",
                             "function and usability issues",
                             "task success and error rates for core tasks in moderated usability tests with target customers"),

                                 "ride, handling or chassis issues",
                                 "ride and handling ratings in structured customer drive clinics against the G60"),
    "POWERTRAIN": Template("performance", "responsive and refined powertrain behaviour",
                           "powertrain behaviour or refinement issues",
                           "customer ratings of power delivery and refinement in drive clinics against the G60"),
    "CHARGING": Template("functional", "reliable and convenient charging",
                         "charging reliability or convenience issues",
                         "charging-session success rate and customer-reported charging issues in field tests"),
    "RANGE_EFFICIENCY": Template("performance", "dependable electric range and trustworthy range information",
                                 "range or range-information issues",
                                 "agreement between displayed and achieved range on defined real-world test routes"),

    "DRIVER_ASSISTANCE": Template("functional_safety_related", "predictable, trustworthy driver-assistance behaviour",
                                  "assistance behaviour or usability issues",

    "SAFETY_SECURITY": Template("safety", "a high perceived and actual level of safety and security",
                                "safety or security concerns",

    "CONNECTIVITY": Template("functional", "reliable phone, app and remote-service connectivity",
                             "connection or app reliability issues",

    "ACCESS": Template("functional", "reliable and convenient vehicle access",
                       "access, key or locking issues",
                       "success rate of locking, unlocking and key/Digital Key operations in field tests"),
    "CLIMATE": Template("comfort", "effective, easy-to-control climate comfort",
                        "climate performance or climate-control issues",

    "EXTERIOR": Template("design", "an attractive, high-quality exterior design and lighting",
                         "exterior design, part or lighting issues",
                         "exterior design and lighting ratings in customer clinics against the G60"),
    "OVERALL": Template("overall", "a convincing overall vehicle", "overall issues",
                        "overall product satisfaction in customer studies against the G60"),
}


class NotGeneratable(ValueError):
    pass


def _focus(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> str:
    if pkg.cluster_level == "vfc_category":
        return f"'{pkg.cluster_label}'"
    if pkg.cluster_level == "extracted_need":
        return f"the need '{pkg.cluster_label}'"
    return f"the {NEED_NAMES[pkg.need_code]} category"


def decide_framing(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """Returns (framing, reasons why refinement is needed)."""
    reasons: list[str] = []
    n = pkg.unique_feedback_count
    if pkg.need_code == "OVERALL":
        reasons.append("The need category 'Overall Vehicle Impression' is too broad for a vehicle requirement.")
    if pkg.cluster_level == "need_category":
        reasons.append("A whole need category spans several VFC classes; select a VFC cluster to identify the affected function.")
    vfc = pkg.vfc_level2_name or ""
    if vfc in CATCH_ALL_VFC or "overall technology" in vfc:
        reasons.append(f"The VFC class '{pkg.cluster_label}' is a broad catch-all and does not identify a specific function.")
    if n < MIN_COMMENTS_FOR_SPECIFIC:
        reasons.append(f"Only {n} direct comments; more evidence is needed before specifying a requirement.")
    g = pkg.label_groups
    if n and g.get("unlabelled", 0) / n > 0.5:
        reasons.append("Most comments have no VFC level-3 label, so the nature of the need is unclear.")
    if reasons:
        return "refine", reasons
    issues, requests, positive = g.get("issue", 0), g.get("request", 0), g.get("positive", 0)
    if issues + requests == 0 or (positive / n >= 0.6 and issues / n < 0.15):
        return "retain", []
    return "improve", []


def _labels_text(pkg: EvidencePackage, group: str, k: int = 3) -> str:
    from services.requirement_evidence import label_group

    items = [l for l in pkg.vfc_level3_labels if label_group(l["label"]) == group][:k]
    return ", ".join(f"'{l['label']}' ({l['unique_feedback_count']} comments)" for l in items)


def _evidence_refs(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> list[EvidenceRef]:
    refs = [EvidenceRef(tier="DIRECT", source_table="feedback", source_key=fid, source_record_id=None,
                        evidence_scope="cluster_member") for fid in pkg.direct_feedback_ids]
    for i in pkg.supporting_evidence + pkg.contextual_evidence:
        refs.append(EvidenceRef(tier=i.tier, source_table={"customer_study": "customer_studies",
                                                           "public_owner_feedback": "public_feedback"}.get(i.kind, "competitor_evidence"),
                                source_key=i.key, source_record_id=i.source.record_id or None, evidence_scope="need_category",
                                requires_review=i.requires_review, note=i.mapping_note))
    for e in pkg.equipment_context:
        refs.append(EvidenceRef(tier="CONTEXTUAL", source_table="equipment", source_key=f"{e.option_code}@p{e.source_page}",
                                source_record_id=e.record_id, evidence_scope="vehicle_catalogue",
                                note="Current G60 option-list offering; not customer evidence."))
    return refs


def allowed_numbers(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> set[str]:
    nums = {str(pkg.unique_feedback_count), str(pkg.classification_count)}
    nums |= {str(v) for v in pkg.label_groups.values()}
    nums |= {str(m["unique_feedback_count"]) for m in pkg.markets}
    nums |= {str(l["unique_feedback_count"]) for l in pkg.vfc_level3_labels}
    nums |= {str(len(pkg.supporting_evidence)), str(len(pkg.contextual_evidence)), str(len(pkg.equipment_context))}
    import re

    nums |= set(re.findall(r"\d+", pkg.cluster_label + " " + " ".join(l["label"] for l in pkg.vfc_level3_labels)))
    nums |= {"5", "60"}  # "5 Series", "G60"
    return nums


def evidence_summary(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> str:
    markets = ", ".join(f"{m['country']} {m['unique_feedback_count']}" for m in pkg.markets[:4])
    g = pkg.label_groups
    publics = sum(i.kind in ("public_owner_feedback", "public_bmw_observation") for i in pkg.supporting_evidence)
    studies = sum(i.kind == "customer_study" for i in pkg.supporting_evidence)
    return (f"DIRECT: {pkg.unique_feedback_count} distinct G60 comments ({pkg.classification_count} classification rows; "
            f"markets {markets}). By original VFC level-3 label group (distinct comments; a comment can be in several): "
            f"issue {g.get('issue', 0)}, request {g.get('request', 0)}, positive {g.get('positive', 0)}. "
            f"SUPPORTING (need-category level, not proof of individual complaints): {publics} public BMW observations, "
            f"{studies} customer-study items. CONTEXTUAL: {len(pkg.contextual_evidence)} competitor observations, "
            f"{len(pkg.equipment_context)} G60 option-list entries.")


def base_assumptions(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> list[str]:
    out = [
        "Customer need is derived from the original BMW VFC category and level-3 labels; no AI analysis of the "
        "comment wording has been performed (counts are from the database).",
        "Target is the next-generation BMW 5 Series; no launch date or model year is assumed.",
        "Supporting evidence (public observations, customer studies) is linked at need-category level and does not "
        "prove any individual complaint; competitor observations are context only.",
        "All acceptance-criterion targets are proposals that require validation by BMW engineering and product "
        "management; no BMW specifications were used or invented.",
    ]
    total = sum(m["unique_feedback_count"] for m in pkg.markets) or 1
    if pkg.markets and pkg.markets[0]["unique_feedback_count"] / total >= 0.8:
        out.append(f"Evidence is concentrated in {pkg.markets[0]['country']} ({pkg.markets[0]['unique_feedback_count']} "
                   f"of {pkg.unique_feedback_count} comments); applicability to other markets must be confirmed.")
    if pkg.mapping_requires_review:
        out.append(f"The VFC-to-need mapping for this cluster requires review: {pkg.mapping_note or 'see Data Quality'}.")
    if pkg.equipment_context:
        out.append("Equipment context reflects the current G60 option list (German market) and indicates offering, "
                   "not customer demand.")
    return out


def generate_rule_based(pkg: EvidencePackage) -> RequirementDraft:
    if pkg.need_code == "OTHER":
        raise NotGeneratable("Comments without a usable VFC classification cannot be turned into a requirement.")
    if pkg.unique_feedback_count == 0:
        raise NotGeneratable("The selection has no direct customer evidence.")
    t = TEMPLATES[pkg.need_code]
    focus = _focus(pkg)
    framing, refine_reasons = decide_framing(pkg)
    g = pkg.label_groups
    issue_labels, request_labels, positive_labels = (_labels_text(pkg, k) for k in ("issue", "request", "positive"))
    assumptions = base_assumptions(pkg)

    if framing == "refine":
        title = f"Refine customer need: {pkg.cluster_label}"
        need = f"To be refined - G60 customers comment on {focus}; the specific underlying need is not yet identified."
        problem = (f"{pkg.unique_feedback_count} G60 comments relate to {focus}. "
                   + (f"Issue labels include {issue_labels}. " if issue_labels else "")
                   + (f"Request labels include {request_labels}. " if request_labels else "")
                   + "The evidence does not yet identify a specific function or failure mode.")
        statement = (f"PROBLEM-ORIENTED DRAFT (requires refinement): The next-generation BMW 5 Series shall address the "
                     f"customer concerns reported for {focus} on the G60. No technical solution is proposed until the "
                     f"specific need has been identified.")
        criteria = [AcceptanceCriterion(
            criterion="The specific customer need and affected function are identified and documented before a "
                      "technical requirement is written.",
            measurement="Review of the cluster's original comments (and AI extraction, if authorised) by product management")]
        rtype = "needs_refinement"
        notes = refine_reasons + ["Missing: which specific function or situation is affected.",
                                  "Missing: whether the need concerns usability, reliability, performance or availability.",
                                  "Missing: analysis of customer wording (AI extraction has not been run)."]
        assumptions.append("This is a problem-oriented placeholder, not a vehicle requirement.")
    elif framing == "retain":
        title = f"Retain valued {pkg.cluster_label}"
        need = f"G60 customers value {t.value} regarding {focus}; this must not regress."
        problem = (f"No dominant problem: {g.get('positive', 0)} of {pkg.unique_feedback_count} comments carry positive "
                   f"VFC labels ({positive_labels})."
                   + (f" {g.get('request', 0)} comments carry request labels ({request_labels})." if g.get("request") else "")
                   + (f" {g.get('issue', 0)} comments carry issue labels ({issue_labels})." if g.get("issue") else ""))
        statement = (f"The next-generation BMW 5 Series shall retain the {t.value} that G60 customers value for {focus}, "
                     f"with no regression relative to the G60.")
        criteria = [
            AcceptanceCriterion(criterion=f"Customer ratings for {focus} are not lower than for the G60.",
                                measurement=t.measurement, target="No regression vs. G60 (proposed - requires validation)"),
            AcceptanceCriterion(criterion=f"Any change to {focus} is reviewed against the G60 comments that praise it.",
                                measurement="Design review referencing the linked direct evidence IDs",
                                target="Review completed (proposed - requires validation)"),
        ]
        rtype, notes = f"retain_{t.requirement_type}", []
        if g.get("request"):
            assumptions.append("Request-labelled comments in this cluster may justify a separate improvement requirement.")
    else:
        title = f"Improve {pkg.cluster_label}"
        need = f"G60 customers need {t.value} regarding {focus}."
        problem = (f"{g.get('issue', 0)} of {pkg.unique_feedback_count} G60 comments carry issue labels"
                   + (f" ({issue_labels})" if issue_labels else "")
                   + (f" and {g.get('request', 0)} carry request labels ({request_labels})" if g.get("request") else "")
                   + f", indicating {t.issue_kind}.")
        statement = (f"The next-generation BMW 5 Series shall provide {t.value} for {focus}, resolving the {t.issue_kind} "
                     f"reported in G60 customer feedback.")
        criteria = [
            AcceptanceCriterion(criterion=f"Fulfilment of the need for {focus} is demonstrated with target customers.",
                                measurement=t.measurement),
            AcceptanceCriterion(criterion=f"Issue-labelled VFC feedback for {focus} is lower than the G60 baseline in "
                                          f"comparable post-launch feedback.",
                                measurement="Distinct comments with issue labels per comparable feedback volume (VFC tracking)",
                                target=f"Baseline: {g.get('issue', 0)} of {pkg.unique_feedback_count} G60 comments in this "
                                       f"export; reduction target proposed - requires validation",
                                target_status="evidence_baseline"),
        ]
        rtype, notes = t.requirement_type, []
        if g.get("positive", 0) / pkg.unique_feedback_count >= 0.3:
            assumptions.append(f"Feedback is mixed: {g.get('positive', 0)} comments also carry positive labels; valued "
                               "aspects must be retained while resolving the issues.")
            criteria.append(AcceptanceCriterion(criterion=f"Aspects of {focus} that G60 customers praise do not regress.",
                                                measurement=t.measurement, target="No regression vs. G60 (proposed - requires validation)"))

    return RequirementDraft(
        title=title, source_cluster_id=pkg.cluster_id, source_insight_id=pkg.insight_id, need_code=pkg.need_code,
        customer_need=need, customer_problem=problem, proposed_requirement=statement, requirement_type=rtype,
        evidence_summary=evidence_summary(pkg), assumptions=assumptions, acceptance_criteria=criteria,
        generation_method="RULE_BASED", template_id=f"{pkg.need_code}:{framing}:v1", framing=framing,
        requires_refinement=framing == "refine", refinement_notes=notes, evidence=_evidence_refs(pkg),
        allowed_numbers=sorted(allowed_numbers(pkg)),
    )

class LLMGateStatus(BaseModel):
    enabled: bool
    reasons: list[str]  # why it is disabled (empty when enabled)


def llm_generation_status(settings: LLMSettings | None = None) -> LLMGateStatus:
    settings = settings or get_llm_settings()
    reasons = []
    if not settings.external_calls_authorized:
        reasons.append("External API use is not authorised (set PRODUCTMIND_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_LLM=true after approval "
                       "to send internal BMW feedback to an external provider).")
    if not (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") or os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN")):
        reasons.append("No API key configured (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).")
    return LLMGateStatus(enabled=not reasons, reasons=reasons)


class LLMCostEstimate(BaseModel):
    model: str
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    estimated_cost_usd: float
    note: str = "Rough estimate (characters / 4); actual cost is logged after the call."


_LLM_SYSTEM = """You help BMW product managers phrase a vehicle requirement for the next-generation BMW 5 Series from evidence.
Write solution-neutral text. Use only the facts provided. Do not invent numbers, statistics, specifications, units,
dates or sources. Do not state that competitors prove anything about BMW customers. Acceptance criteria must name a
measurement method; leave targets as proposals requiring validation."""

_LLM_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "title": {"type": "string"}, "customer_need": {"type": "string"}, "customer_problem": {"type": "string"},
        "proposed_requirement": {"type": "string"}, "assumptions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "acceptance_criteria": {"type": "array", "items": {
            "type": "object", "properties": {"criterion": {"type": "string"}, "measurement": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["criterion", "measurement"], "additionalProperties": False}},
    },
    "required": ["title", "customer_need", "customer_problem", "proposed_requirement", "assumptions", "acceptance_criteria"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}


def _llm_payload(pkg: EvidencePackage, base: RequirementDraft) -> str:
    return json.dumps({
        "rule_based_draft": base.model_dump(include={"title", "customer_need", "customer_problem", "proposed_requirement"}),
        "facts": {"need": pkg.need_name, "cluster": pkg.cluster_label, "unique_comments": pkg.unique_feedback_count,
                  "label_groups": pkg.label_groups, "vfc_level3_labels": pkg.vfc_level3_labels[:8]},
        "example_comments": [{"id": d.feedback_id, "text": d.text} for d in pkg.direct_evidence[:10]],
    }, ensure_ascii=False)


def estimate_llm_cost(pkg: EvidencePackage, settings: LLMSettings | None = None) -> LLMCostEstimate:
    from services.llm_client import LLMUsage, estimate_cost_usd

    settings = settings or get_llm_settings()
    base = generate_rule_based(pkg)
    usage = LLMUsage(input_tokens=(len(_LLM_SYSTEM) + len(_llm_payload(pkg, base))) // 4, output_tokens=1500)
    return LLMCostEstimate(model=settings.model, input_tokens=usage.input_tokens, output_tokens=usage.output_tokens,
                           estimated_cost_usd=estimate_cost_usd(settings.model, usage))


class LLMNotAuthorized(PermissionError):
    pass


def generate_llm_assisted(pkg: EvidencePackage, *, confirmed: bool, cost_acknowledged: LLMCostEstimate | None,
                          settings: LLMSettings | None = None, client=None) -> RequirementDraft:
    """Gated LLM rewrite of the rule-based draft. Raises LLMNotAuthorized unless
    every condition holds. ``client`` lets tests inject a fake (no network)."""
    settings = (settings or get_llm_settings()).model_copy(update={"use_fallbacks": False})
    gate = llm_generation_status(settings)
    if client is None and not gate.enabled:
        raise LLMNotAuthorized("; ".join(gate.reasons))
    if not settings.external_calls_authorized:
        raise LLMNotAuthorized("External API use is not authorised.")
    if not confirmed or cost_acknowledged is None:
        raise LLMNotAuthorized("The user must review the cost estimate and explicitly confirm generation.")
    if client is None:
        from services.llm_client import AnthropicLLMClient

        client = AnthropicLLMClient(settings)  # fallbacks forced off above
    base = generate_rule_based(pkg)
    response = client.complete_json(system=_LLM_SYSTEM, user=_llm_payload(pkg, base), schema=_LLM_SCHEMA,
                                    max_tokens=settings.max_tokens)
    if response.stop_reason == "refusal" or not response.text:
        raise RuntimeError("The model returned no usable draft; keep the rule-based draft.")
    data = json.loads(response.text)
    return base.model_copy(update={
        "title": data["title"], "customer_need": data["customer_need"], "customer_problem": data["customer_problem"],
        "proposed_requirement": data["proposed_requirement"],
        "assumptions": base.assumptions + [a for a in data["assumptions"] if a not in base.assumptions]
                       + ["Text drafted with LLM assistance from the facts above; review wording against the evidence."],
        "acceptance_criteria": [AcceptanceCriterion(criterion=c["criterion"], measurement=c["measurement"])
                                for c in data["acceptance_criteria"]] or base.acceptance_criteria,
        "generation_method": "LLM_ASSISTED", "template_id": None,
    })
